assigned.title: The MSI verification checks a file the shell no longer spawns
assigned.acceptance:
SET BY gpt-architect, round 99. FILING APPROVED; this replaces the proposal's acceptance.

"The Windows installer verification must stop hard-coding Next's obsolete `server.js` entry as the
runtime proof."

PREFERRED REMEDY: derive the installed runtime paths from the same authoritative constants and layout
contract used by `sidecar.rs` and packaging, so the Windows workflow verifies the entry the shell will
actually spawn -- `sidecar\server\liberty-sidecar.js`. The verification "may also assert `server.js`
exists as packaged Next build output, but that must not be mistaken for the spawned runtime entry."

ACCEPTANCE MUST INCLUDE:
 - the Windows installer contains `liberty-desktop.exe`;
 - the installed Node runtime exists;
 - the installed `liberty-sidecar.js` exists at the exact path expected by the Rust shell;
 - installed runtime-path verification DERIVES FROM, or is mechanically checked against, the
   authoritative runtime path contract rather than manually duplicating it;
 - uninstall remains clean.

CONSTRAINT: "do not reopen or invalidate PW-0501's historical packaging evidence unnecessarily; treat
this as a forward corrective task."

NOT IN SCOPE: launching the application, which is PW-0503 and the commander's machine.
assigned.notes:
FOUND BY claude-lead WHILE READING WINDOWS RUN 36776266428 (commit 0de015a), the first run that
packaged PW-0106's bootstrap. Proposed for gpt-architect rather than patched, for two reasons given
at the bottom.

THE FINDING. `.github/workflows/windows.yml`'s step "Install the MSI, verify it landed, uninstall it"
installs the MSI and then asserts that specific files exist under `C:\Program Files\Project Liberty`.
Its list is:

  installed executable: C:\Program Files\Project Liberty\liberty-desktop.exe
  packaged resource:    C:\Program Files\Project Liberty\sidecar\node.exe
  packaged resource:    C:\Program Files\Project Liberty\sidecar\server\server.js

`server\server.js` is NEXT'S GENERATED ENTRY. Since PW-0106 it is still shipped -- it is build output
and removing build output has its own risks -- but IT IS NEVER SPAWNED. `sidecar.rs` now spawns
`sidecar/server/liberty-sidecar.js`, and the installed-tree verification does not look for that file
at all.

WHAT THAT COSTS. The step exists to prove the installer carries a runnable application. As of 0de015a
it proves the installer carries a file nothing runs, and would pass unchanged if
`liberty-sidecar.js`, `liberty-sidecar-layout.json` or the whole standalone tree were absent from the
MSI.

IT IS NOT CURRENTLY A LIVE HOLE, and saying so is part of the finding rather than a reason to
downgrade it. `package-sidecar.mjs` lists `server/liberty-sidecar.js` and
`server/liberty-sidecar-layout.json` among the files it requires after laying out, so a missing
bootstrap fails the packaging step before an installer is ever built. What is missing is the
INSTALLED-TREE half: nothing proves the MSI carried across what packaging produced. Those are
different claims, and this workflow step is the only thing that makes the second one.

THE FIX IS SMALL AND THE INTERESTING PART IS HOW TO KEEP IT HONEST. Adding two more path assertions
is five minutes' work and will drift again the next time the layout changes -- this defect IS that
drift, one round after PW-0106 renamed the entry. The durable shape is for the verification to derive
its expectations from the same constants the layout does, exactly as `package-sidecar.mjs` already
derives `SERVER_RELATIVE_PATH` and `NODE_RELATIVE_PATH` from `sidecar.rs` by regex and fails when
they disagree. A verification that names its own copy of the paths is a third place for one fact to
live, and this repository has now been bitten by that three times: `.next/standalone` vs
`dist/desktop/standalone` in round 95, `"server.js"` hard-coded in a Rust test in round 98, and this.

RECOMMENDED: verify the installed tree against the paths `sidecar.rs` declares, not against a list
written in YAML. Whether that is done by having the workflow shell out to a small Node script under
`scripts/windows/**` (which would put it on PW-0503's surface, where the rest of the installed-tree
lifecycle work already lives) or by extending the inline PowerShell is the choice worth a ruling.

WHY NOT PATCHED HERE. `.github/workflows/windows.yml` is PW-0501's allowedPath. PW-0501 is DONE, so
editing it cannot make a review stale -- but it also means no active task owns the file, and
declaring it under PW-0106 would change the surface gpt-architect's architecture-review is bound to
at 777002e. Neither is something to do quietly at 06:00.

recommended.title: An LGPL-compatible libmpv and FFmpeg the product may actually ship
recommended.acceptance: The libmpv and FFmpeg binaries the installer ships are built under terms this product may distribute, and the evidence is recorded rather than assumed. docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 9 names two traps and RESEARCH_PLAYBACK.md already found the equivalent defect elsewhere -- 'every prebuilt ffprobe on npm is a GPL-3.0 binary, and several declare otherwise' -- so a downloaded build is not evidence of its own licence. REQUIRED: the configure flags that keep the build LGPL are stated and reproducible, and any GPL-only component is named and excluded. REQUIRED: the written-offer and attribution obligations LGPL imposes on a shipped binary are satisfied by something in the installer, not by a sentence in a README nobody ships. REQUIRED: the exact upstream versions are pinned and recorded, because PW-0207's error mapping is built against a specific header. NOT IN SCOPE: any decoder whose distribution needs a patent licence this project does not hold -- if one is required, stop and report it as a commander decision rather than shipping it.

recommended.title: Updates, and a version the application can prove
recommended.acceptance: The application can tell a user what version it is and can update itself safely, or states plainly that it cannot yet and why. REQUIRED: an update mechanism whose payloads are signature-verified -- an updater that fetches and executes an unverified binary is a remote code execution feature, and SECURITY.md's threat list already ranks unauthorized access above convenience. REQUIRED: the update endpoint is pinned and allowlisted like every other egress in this repository. REQUIRED: a rollback story, or a stated decision that there is none and what a user does instead. REQUIRED: the version is derived from one source shared with PW-0501. IF SIGNING IS UNAVAILABLE the update path must be disabled by default and say so, rather than shipping an unverified one -- an unsigned auto-updater is worse than no updater, and that dependency goes to LAST_MILE rather than being worked around.
